fullText:
The new iPhone 18 Pro and 18 Pro Max have been out for a week, and they have been amazing devices to use and test. While the actual footprint and visual design remain unchanged, Apple spiced things up with new colors like Glacier, Burgundy, and a true Deep Black version. These colors are a nice new addition to the iPhone lineup, but, of course, the main question I get asked is: What case should I get to protect my new $ 1,200+ device? Luckily, there are already hundreds of case options for the new 18 Pro lineup, and I have been lucky enough to test a bunch. I know cases are purely subjective and a matter of preference, but I figured I would share some of my favorites!

Be sure to check out our hands-on video with all of these cases to see which one would be best for you!

Pitaka Edge case

I have always leaned towards ultra-thin and minimal cases. I like being able to protect my iPhone while still feeling its actual design. If thinness and lightweight cases are what you are into then Pitaka’s Edge cases are the first option I would consider. You get:

Ultra-thin and lightweight aramid fiber construction

Improved camera protection with a raised camera lip and PitaTap camera control cover

Built-in MagSafe magnets for added strength

Precise cutouts for the buttons, speakers, and USB-C port

Available in a ton of different designs

Even at just 20g and 1mm in thickness, this case offers a ton of protection and rigidity. Pitaka’s Edge case is available today on Amazon for $59 and comes in 10+ colors and designs. 

Nomad Sport Case

Nomad’s Sport Case gives you that perfect balance of everyday protection while staying relatively thin and lightweight. I went with the Lunar Gret color to contrast with the Deep Black iPhone, and it looks fantastic. This case brings:

Smooth, soft-touch exterior with a protective construction

Tactile metal buttons with a textured finish

Microfiber interior lining to help protect your iPhone

Raised camera and screen edges for additional protection

Built-in MagSafe compatibility and a dedicated Camera Control cover

If you want a high-quality, no-frills case that keeps your phone protected while still making it look awesome, I would look into the Nomad Sport case. It’s available on Amazon for $55!

Xtremm Inno E-Ink Case

This is easily one of the most unique and fun cases that I have ever reviewed. The Xtremm Inno  puts a color E-Ink display on the rear of the iPhone that is 100% customizable. You can put any image you want on there, like family photos, team logos, anime characters, literally anything. It’s all done via NFC, so the case does not need a battery, power, or Bluetooth, keeping it as thin and light as any other regular case. It feels like magic. 

Customizable color E-Ink display on the back of the case

NFC technology for transferring images from your iPhone

Support for personal photos and AI-generated designs

Raised camera protection and dedicated Camera Control cover

Built-in MagSafe compatibility despite the rear display

We have a whole video on this to show it off. I recommend watching it before purchasing, just to see how cool this looks! It’s available on Amazon for $75 and comes in five different colors for the new iPhone 18 Pro lineup. 

Rokform Crystal Case

Now, if you need something a bit more rugged with added protection but still want to show off that new burgundy iPhone color, then Rokform is a great choice. Not only is it extremely protective, but It Also has Rokform’s proprietary locking system in addition to MagSafe. This makes it even more useful for someone who needs to securely mount their iPhone on a bike, motorcycle, or other devices that require more than just magnets. 

Rugged construction with reinforced corners and raised edges

Transparent back panel that shows off your iPhone’s color

Rokform’s proprietary twist-lock mounting system

Built-in MagSafe compatibility

Full camera plateau protection with a dedicated Camera Control cover

The Rokform Crystal Case is available on Amazon for $69. They also have their own ecosystem of mounts and attachments worth checking out. 

BodyGuardz Weave Case

This is a brand that I had not heard much about until this year. They have been around for a while, but they just released their new Weave line, and I love the design, texture, and multifunctionality of it all. You get:

Textured woven exterior with a comfortable grip

Integrated kickstand 

Speaker channels designed to direct audio forward

Raised edges for screen and camera protection

Built-in MagSafe 

The speaker directional feature is something I had not seen before, and it actually makes a nice difference. Because of how the speaker cutout is designed, it directs the audio right at you rather than to your left or right. Very unique touch! The BodyGuardz Weave is available on Amazon for $59

Andar Aspen

If you are someone who misses the old iPhone leather cases of years past, then Andar is the next best alternative. I have been using their cases for years, and they are some of the best leather cases on the market. You get:

Genuine leather exterior that develops a unique patina over time and smells fantastic 

Soft microfiber interior lining 

Raised edges around the display and camera for additional protection

Dedicated Camera Control cover and tactile metal buttons

Built-in MagSafe compatibility and multiple color options

Their new black color matches the Deep Black iPhone so well that it almost makes the iPhone disappear in the shadows. They have over 10 colors to choose from, and these cases just get better with time. The Andar Aspen Case is available for $70 and can be purchased directly through Andar.

Spigen Nano Pop Case

Spigen’s Nano Pop case is a great option if you are looking for something that will color-match and enhance your new iPhone. It has a two-tone design that looks especially nice with the new Burgundy iPhone, and it also has uniquely textured sides for additional grip in the hand. The Pop case gives you:

Two-tone design with contrasting colors

Flexible, rubberized construction with textured sides for additional grip

Raised edges and protection around the entire camera plateau

Dedicated Camera Control cover

Built-in lanyard attachment point

This one is the most budget-friendly of the bunch as well, sitting at just $21 directly from Amazon

Final take

As I mentioned in the intro, cases are highly subjective purchases. It is almost like clothing but for your phone. There is no right or wrong answer to any of these, just a matter of what you think works and looks best. All of these have their own unique selling points and differentiators, and they come from very reputable brands, so there is no going wrong with any of them. I personally like to keep it as thin and light as possible, while I know my brother likes his cases bulky and protective. 

Be sure to catch our video on these, as we go hands-on with all of these cases, and leave a comment on some other brands I need to check out. I would love to give you guys a round two of my favorite cases later in the year. For those people waiting for the iPhone Duo, we will also have something similar for the new device.

snippet: Oppo has just held its launch of the Find X10 series in its home region of China, with a global launch to come for the new devices. more…
fullText:
Oppo has just held its launch of the Find X10 series in its home region of China, with a global launch to come for the new devices.

We’ve already heard a ton about the Oppo Find X10 series through leaks and teasers, but today’s launch in China unveils everything these new phones bring to the table. Oppo has three devices here, starting with its flagship Find X10 Pro Max.

This is the device Oppo has been teasing a triple 200MP camera setup for, with the Find X10 Pro Max using 200MP sensors for its main (f/1.5, 24mm), ultrawide (f/2.2, 13mm, 124-degree FOV), and telephoto (f/2.1, 70mm, 3x optical zoom) lenses. Oppo touts that you can shoot in 8K across all of the rear cameras. There’s also a 50MP front-facing camera.

Find X10 Pro Max runs on MediaTek’s Dimensity 9600 Pro chipset paired with 12GB or 16GB of RAM, up to 1TB of UFS 4.1 storage, and ColorOS 17 (Android 17) out of the box. It has a 6.78-inch display – the same size as last year – with an in-display fingerprint sensor. Powering the whole show is an 8,000 mAh battery with 80W/67W wired/wireless charging.

	

The standard Find X10 is a step down in only a handful of ways, using the same chipset and battery and still packing two 200MP cameras. Find X10 E makes further cuts for a lower price point.

title: Apple Pay just got even better with four new features and more
snippet: Apple Pay is a go-to feature for iPhone users when shopping in stores, online, and in apps. Apple recently announced four new features that make Apple Pay even better. Here’s how they work, plus one major expansion that’s rolling out now. more…
fullText:
Apple Pay is a go-to feature for iPhone users when shopping in stores, online, and in apps. Apple recently announced four new features that make Apple Pay even better. Here’s how they work, plus one major expansion that’s rolling out now. 

New design in iOS 27

One of my favorite changes in iOS 27 is the redesigned Apple Pay checkout interface. The new interface makes it much easier to switch between different cards during the checkout flow on websites and in apps.

In the new design, you can easily swipe between cards on the main Apple Pay checkout screen. You can also tap on a card to view a grid of all your available Apple Pay cards.

The design also makes it easier to see information about individual cards, including rewards, balances, pay later options, and more.

iOS 27 was released to everyone last week. You can update in the Settings app on your iPhone. 

American Express rewards

Apple and American Express recently announced a new partnership that lets you pay with American Express rewards points.

When shopping online or in apps with an American Express card, you’ll see a new “Use Rewards” option alongside your available Membership Rewards points balance. You can apply points to cover all or part of your purchase, right in the Apple Pay checkout flow.

American Express points redeemed via Apple Pay are valued at 0.7 cents each. For example, this means 10,000 points can be redeemed for $70 applied towards your purchase.

In iOS 27, Apple is adding a new “Tap to Share” feature that integrates with Apple Pay on iPhone for in-store shopping.

This feature is an extension of Tap to Pay on iPhone. Apple explains:

With just a tap, customers can connect to a participating merchant’s iPhone for a more personalized and faster in-store purchase experience that allows for secure sharing of information, such as email and other contact information, shipping address, loyalty rewards information, and more.

Customers will also be able to view the items in their basket in real time so they can keep track of what they’ve purchased and ensure all sales and discounts are properly applied.

When done, shoppers can complete the checkout on their iPhone using Apple Pay.

Reload debit cards

iPhone users with select banks can manage their debit card balances directly in the Apple Pay interface. According to Apple, you’ll be able to use Apple Pay to add money to a supported debit card directly in Apple Wallet or when checking out.

Bonus: Apple Pay at Walmart 

This one isn’t really a new feature developed by Apple. Instead, it’s something that should’ve happened years ago finally coming to fruition. Walmart has announced that it is finally starting to roll out support for Apple Pay. Apple Pay is also rolling out to Sam’s Club as part of this initiative.  

Walmart started rolling out Apple Pay (and broader contactless support) this week in Arkansas. The retailer says it launch for all stores in the United States by the end of this year. 

Wrap up

As Apple Pay continues to increase in popularity and prevalence among retailers, it’s great to see Apple continue to improve the experience. Personally, Apple Pay is my checkout payment method of choice basically everywhere I shop — whether that’s online or in store.

Apple today announced that Tap to Pay on iPhone is now available in eight additional Latin American countries, with support from six payment platforms across the region. Here are the details.

Tap to Pay on iPhone expands to eight new countries

In an update published to its Latin America and the Caribbean Newsroom, Apple announced today an expansion of Tap to Pay on iPhone across Argentina, Colombia, Costa Rica, the Dominican Republic, Guatemala, Honduras, Panama, and Peru.

Tap to Pay on iPhone allows merchants to accept in-person contactless payments using only a compatible iPhone and supported payment app, without the need for additional card readers or payment terminals.

Here’s the list of countries and payment platforms gaining support today:

Argentina: Mercado Pago

Colombia: SumUp, Symbiotic

Costa Rica: Geopagos, Symbiotic, Visa Acceptance Solutions

Dominican Republic: Azul, Visa Acceptance Solutions

Guatemala: Geopagos, Symbiotic

Honduras: Geopagos, Symbiotic

Panama: Geopagos, Symbiotic

Peru: SumUp

Apple also noted that Tap to Pay on iPhone “is compatible with contactless debit and credit cards from major payment networks, including American Express, Mastercard, and Visa.”

Apple originally announced Tap to Pay on iPhone on February 8, 2022. It was initially announced for the United States, with Stripe as the first payment platform set to support it.

Since then, it has expanded to 59 countries and regions, with Apple’s current list naming more than 100 payment service providers worldwide, including today’s additions.

For almost 30 years, Jason Kottke has been one of my main sources for interesting content on (and off) the internet that I would most certainly have never discovered otherwise.

A few days ago, he published this post, linking to Apple’s Dimensional Drawings section inside the Accessories area of its developer website.

The list also includes products like the MacBook Neo and the Siri Remote, as well as accessories such as AirTag, AirPods charging cases, and even the Apple Vision Pro’s ZEISS Optical Inserts.

Each document includes precise measurements for everything from the device’s overall dimensions and curves to its buttons, cameras, sensors, speakers, and connectors, along with detailed keepout zones and instructions showing where certain materials should not be placed.

While these documents are meant for accessory makers, they’re also likely to appeal to anyone with even a mild interest in hardware, industrial design, or simply the kind of attention to detail that generally draws people to Apple products in the first place.

Apple TV users have long been able to set HomePods as speakers for audio output. But tvOS 27.2 looks poised to offer a big upgrade, with HomePod surround sound now available in the beta.

Update: Following publication, leaker pdfu posted on X that the feature referenced below is in tvOS 27.0 and isn’t actually for surround sound yet, despite additional evidence of the feature in 27.2 code. Original article below.

tvOS 27.2 beta 2 supports using four HomePods at once as speakers

Earlier this month, it was discovered that HomePod 27 beta 8 included references to a forthcoming surround sound feature for Apple TV. 

Now as spotted by FlatpanelsHD, that feature has made an appearance in tvOS 27.2 beta 2.

We've examined tvOS 27.2 beta 2 and the rumored 4x HomePod wireless surround pairing with Apple TV 4K is now implemented, as shown below.

However, it's not yet fully baked, as there is currently no way to assign roles to each HomePod pair, i.e. front and rear speakers. It works… https://t.co/cufeJwx0PQ pic.twitter.com/IG3uqH32NU

— FlatpanelsHD (@Flatpanels) September 23, 2026

As seen in the screenshot above, the Apple TV 4K running tvOS 27.2 is configured to send audio to four HomePods total—two full-size models and two HomePod minis.

More details are shared by Rasmus Larsen on FlatpanelsHD’s website:

Via the Home app, you can now pair two sets of HomePods, four in total, wirelessly to Apple TV 4K. However, the feature is not yet fully baked, as you cannot assign roles to the four speakers, for example rear speakers – they play the same audio from the front and rear. It works with Atmos and surround sound from video sources, but menu and game audio only plays through the front speakers.

	

It’s been widely rumored for some time that Apple is working on a big overhaul and expansion of its Home product line. A new ‘HomePad’ device along with new Apple TV 4K and HomePod models are expected to launch in October.

Surround sound could be a great addition for HomePod and Apple TV users. But it’s also likely a good sign that Apple will indeed launch new Home products soon.

fullText:
Good morning. Today I’m bumping to Carly Rae Jepsen’s new double album (it’s great!), wishing I had more kidneys so I could afford the new M5 Ultra Mac Studio, marveling at Astra’s ability to decrypt 100-year-old WWI cyphers, and counting down the days until I can play Control Resonant.

As a reminder, Inbox is the tech newsletter that goes beyond the news cycle. We cover the most important 9to5Google stories from the last couple of days along with a few highlights from around the web. We publish every Tuesday and Thursday, and if you like what you read, please subscribe.

Inbox is written by Daniel Bader. Read previous issues here, and then catch up with Ben Schoon’s excellent Weekender column published every Sunday.

⭐️ Starred

I’ve been covering Google’s multifarious hardware endeavors for nearly 20 years, from the early days of Nexus phones through this week’s Googlebook unveiling, and I see a few important parallels. Google has always wanted to assert some measure of control over the user experience, but that amount has ebbed and flowed depending on where its product sits in the funnel. 

	

The early days of Android were about growth, which meant leveraging established players like LG, Samsung, Huawei, and others to build its hardware while promulgating a free and open-source operating system that quickly supplanted giants like Nokia and Microsoft.

Alongside Android, Google nurtured Chrome OS (which later became, confusingly, ChromeOS) as its laptop (and occasional desktop) operating system, that, like Android, became synonymous with cheap-and-cheerful hardware, particularly in schools. And while Google did the work to rid itself of that budget reputation on the phone side (though, arguably, Samsung did the bulk of the heavy lifting), it never really managed to do the same on ChromeOS despite numerous attempts to build premium hardware.

Now, ChromeOS is being replaced by Googlebook, and its main appeal is quite simple to understand: “Hey premium Android users, we see you. Here’s a product that can bring you Apple users’ ecosystem benefits while retaining the openness and diversity of Android.”

A few questions jump to mind when I hear that:

Yes, there are billions of Android users out there, but are enough of them clamoring for ecosystem unity to replace their existing laptops in order to entwine their lives even further with Google?

Is that ecosystem unity actually additive in the same way that Apple has proven with iOS and macOS, or will it be more like the way Microsoft has tried to harmonize Android and iOS devices with Windows?

Will the legacy of Google killing off seemingly healthy products turn people away from Googlebooks?

Is this objectively the worst time to launch a new hardware brand?

Also interesting is that Google’s own hardware is absent from this ecosystem launch. Like Chromebooks before them, Googlebooks will be made by familiar companies like Lenovo, Dell, Acer, and ASUS, with internals from Intel, Qualcomm, and soon AMD — another reminder that Google is playing a very particular role here, that of software and AI vendor.

That Gemini Intelligence integration, which has been teased from the start of the Googlebook announcement, is another differentiator not only from macOS and Windows, but also from Chromebooks. Google is positioning the Googlebook as the best place to interact with Gemini, whose increasingly agentic aspirations now tap into every corner of Google’s product lineup. But it’s also appealing to developers and vibe-coders alike with a native Antigravity app and 12 months of Google AI Pro, a subscription that comes with a substantial amount of coding credit.

So is a Googlebook for Android users who want to code? Is it for fans of ChromeOS who want more integration with their phones? Is it for the Android faithful, the diehards who have been waiting patiently for their turn in the ecosystem sun? 

We don’t have long to wait: Googlebooks hit the market early next month.

✉️ Inbox

The camera is my favorite part of smart glasses, but it just feels wrong now. Ben’s Weekender essay grapples with the realities of being a glasshole in 2026.

Roku adding new apps & subscription bundles, homescreen redesign expanding. Could Roku’s smart TV OS get any more bloated and ad-infested? Of course it could.

Galaxy Z Fold 8 saw a surge in popularity as soon as Apple unveiled the iPhone Duo. No doubt that’s why Samsung wanted to get ahead of the iPhone Duo’s release.

Honor confirms list of devices getting its Liquid Glass-filled Android 17 update [Video]. This is egregious, even for Honor.

Google ‘AI contribution pilot’ tests paying websites when they’re used in AI results. Any more money for publishers is a good thing, but I doubt this will end with more money for journalism over the long term.

Google goes in-depth, and a bit NSFW, on Noto 3D emoji as Android rollout expands. I love these so, so much.

Motorola confirms ‘Signature 27’ debut next week alongside new Snapdragon chips. It’s giving old-school Droid Razr in the best way possible. This will be the first ‘Signature’ phone to come to the US.

Motorola teases high-end ‘Signature 27’ with a wild-looking design

Clicks Communicator lands in December with 12GB RAM, two months of free data. We feature Clicks’ Kevin and Jeff in this week’s Sideload episode, and it was a really fun conversation.

Samsung’s battery upgrades for Galaxy S27 Ultra and Pro leak – is it enough? More silicon, please.

Gemini app for macOS adding send and read iMessage integration. ChatGPT did it first, but it’s still not a feature I’d recommend enabling if you want your messages to stay private.

Gmail adds ‘Copy code’ shortcut for 2FA on Android & iOS. This is super handy, and I feel like I’m going to use it all the time.

Google confirms Gemini hacked into three companies during cybersecurity test months ago. Apparently this happened in May, but Google didn’t report it because the agents didn’t do anything wrong.

Here’s the OnePlus 16 that you probably won’t be able to buy [Video]. Womp, womp.

Xiaomi 18 Pro has a Privacy Display that does more than Galaxy S26 Ultra, launches this week [Video]. This phone looks about as over-the-top as you can get (complimentary).

Apple didn’t give up on stylus support for iPhone Duo; Samsung’s Galaxy Z Fold should take notes. Amen.

All about Googlebooks

Google fully details Googlebooks: $899+, October launch, & more

Googlebook OS hands-on: It’s Android, stupid

Googlebook hands-on: What makes a laptop, a laptop? [Video]

What do you actually use a laptop for, and would Googlebook be able to do it? [Poll]

MediaTek’s flagship laptop chip is the Dimensity CX C10 Max, debuts in a Lenovo Googlebook.

🤝 Cc: Kevin Michaluk

Welcome to a new project I’m calling Cc:, where I ask interesting people in the community about what’s making them happy both inside and outside the world of tech. This week, I’m speaking with Kevin Michaluk, Clicks co-founder and former BlackBerry superuser.

Who are you?

Kevin Michaluk aka @crackberrykevin / CBK

What do you do for work?

How It Started: Founder at CrackBerry.com & Mobile Nations (spent 15 years in tech media); How It’s Going: Founder & President at Clicks Technology.

What do you do for fun?

Depends on the season! This summer picked up golf again (my obsession in my teenage years) and pickleball for the first time. I spend so much time working that some physical activities out of the house/office and away from screens for a few hours a week feels like a necessity for my mental and physical health.

What is your relationship like with technology these days?

More intentional than ever. I wrote the first book on Smartphone Addiction back in 2008 and have been more acutely aware than most of the detrimental effects on individuals and society that smartphones, social media and tech can have. That’s part of the reason we launched Clicks in 2024 and Communicator this year. We’re building purpose built tech that helps people restore some of that balance with tech by building tools that respect their time. It’s not about being overly restrictive, but building experiences that people love and ideally lead to a healthier relationship with their tech. 

What are a few apps you can’t live without and why?

Whoop – I’ve had an on again / off again with fitness trackers over the years and have literally used them all… but this past year have grown to really love and rely on my Whoop. I jive more with their use of recovery score and strain goals over step count goals or trying to close rings, and I like that they have accessories to wear the tracker in. Sleeping with a ring or band on my wrist annoys me and ruins my sleep – with Whoop I literally own several pairs of their “Whoop underwear” that I put the tracker in and wear to bed. And as a guy who loves wearing real watches, I just don’t like wearing a smartwatch on my wrist that could be better occupied by a mechanical watch. And even Whoop’s new AI Chat feature I use more than I thought I would… it’s come in real handy for when I’m traveling internationally and trying to map out the best sleep and workout schedules to help me balance the time zone changes.

Shopify – I mean, when you’re building a company and one of your biggest sales channels is DTC, it’s hard not to spend a LOT of time in Shopify. 

TOP SECRET – No, that’s not the name of the app… but ask me about it again in early 2027 and I’ll share the details on the newest app I’m using that I actually can’t live without. title: iOS 27 lets you create your own custom iPhone wallpapers
snippet: Apple introduces new iPhone wallpapers every year, and you can download iOS 27’s additions here. But iOS 27 also adds the ability to create your own custom wallpapers. Here’s how. more…
fullText:
Apple introduces new iPhone wallpapers every year, and you can download iOS 27’s additions here. But iOS 27 also adds the ability to create your own custom wallpapers. Here’s how.

Here’s how you can create custom wallpapers in iOS 27

This year as part of iOS 27’s overall theme of major AI improvements, Apple has given its Image Playground app an overhaul.

Image Playground now offers more powerful image generation capabilities and far fewer restrictions than before. It even lets you create images that are the perfect wallpaper size.

But you don’t even need to open the Image Playground app to create wallpapers.

iOS 27 lets you create your own iPhone wallpapers right from the wallpaper picker.

Go to Settings ⇾ Wallpaper ⇾ Add New Wallpaper or long-press your Lock Screen and hit the ‘+’ button to open iOS 27’s wallpaper gallery.

New in the gallery this year, you’ll see Image Playground as an option in the top row. iOS 27 also automatically adds some AI-generated images to the Featured wallpaper section.

For example, you’ll see suggested wallpapers that are based on your own photos, but in a new style. 

In my testing of iOS 27, with no effort on my part, my iPhone prepared beautifully stylized versions of some of my favorite photos that look great as wallpapers.

Wherever you see an AI-generated wallpaper in the gallery, Apple’s new Image Playground icon appears next to it. That way, it’s always clear where the image came from.

If you like one of Apple’s suggested AI wallpapers, you can choose it and be all set.

But iOS 27 also lets you create fully custom wallpapers by hitting the Image Playground button in the top row. Image Playground will ask you to describe your image, and let you optionally choose a style or base it on an existing photo or person.

When the image is created, it’s automatically the perfect size for an iPhone wallpaper.

title: Googlebooks will get full GeForce Now support ‘later this year’
snippet: Nvidia says Google’s new Gemini-infused laptops are slated to get GeForce Now support before the year is up, which is perfect because Googlebooks don’t exactly pack a ton of power. more…
fullText:
Nvidia says Google’s new Gemini-infused laptops are slated to get GeForce Now support before the year is up, which is perfect because Googlebooks don’t exactly pack a ton of power.

The entire Googlebook line was officially announced on September 21, spanning across Acer, Dell, ASUS, HP, and Lenovo. Each has its own draw, but they share the same baseline 16GB of RAM, up to 32GB. Each is equipped with a touchscreen and made from “premium materials,” and they genuinely look great. What qualifies as “premium” ranges from aluminum to carbon fiber. Of course, each has the instantly iconic Glowbar somewhere on the cover, flashing when the laptop is opened or closed.

In essence, Googlebooks run Android, for better or worse. Googlebook OS is almost a parallel operating system, but it and mobile Android go hand-in-hand by design. By nature, that means Google didn’t intend to pack these with discrete graphics cards that could power most games. But that’s why GeForce Now exists, right?

Nvidia announced that GeForce Now would be coming to Googlebooks in an official capacity before the year is up. The original statement only specifies it will arrive “later this year,” which leaves a gap of around three months.

	

That doesn’t mean GeForce Now won’t work with Googlebooks when they become available in October. Google Chrome and even Firefox now support GeForce Now natively through the browser. That means logging into the game streaming website will present a similar experience to a fully dedicated Googlebook app.

Still, an app will likely be a better experience tailored to the hardware outfit Google and its partners pack into the new laptops.

This was expected for a couple of reasons. Google has partnered with Nvidia in the past, and Chromebooks were one of the main targets for GeForce Now in the early days. On top of that, when Googlebooks were first shown off, the majority of titles seen were via GeForce Now and not running on native hardware.

GeForce Now also announced today that a slew of new titles are getting support this week:

Stick It to the Stickman

CONTROL Resonant

Wild West Pioneers

DragonSword: Awakening

Everything Is Crab

LEGO Batman: Legacy of The Dark Knight

title: Honor Magic 9 Pro Max goes official with 8,800 mAh battery, ARRI cameras, Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6
snippet: Honor has officially announced its latest flagship in China, with the Honor Magic 9 Pro Max packing powerful specs, upgraded cameras, the latest Snapdragon chip, and confirmed for an global launch later on. more…
fullText:
Honor has officially announced its latest flagship in China, with the Honor Magic 9 Pro Max packing powerful specs, upgraded cameras, the latest Snapdragon chip, and confirmed for an global launch later on.

The Honor Magic 9 Pro Max is an all-out flagship with a heavy focus on its cameras, so let’s start there.

Continuing its ARRI partnership that debuted on the Robot Phone, the Magic 9 Pro Max packs a 200MP main camera with “gimbal-level stabilization,” a 200MP telephoto camera with 3.5x optical zoom, and a 50MP ultra-wide camera. Those are arranged on the back in the style of an ARRI cinema camera, and they’re also tuned by ARRI to produce better colors both in photos and videos. Honor is also building out additional hardware including two teleconverter lenses and a “Mobile Video Kit” in partnership with SmallRig.

The front-facing camera is no slouch either, with a 55MP sensor that’s paired with a 3D depth sensing camera for face unlock.

	

The phone surrounding those cameras packs a punch too. 

Honor Magic 9 Pro Max is powered by the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 and starts at 12GB of RAM and 256GB of storage. Honor is using its own “Imaging Chip H1” to enhance camera processing, with MagicOS 11 based on Android 17 also available out of the box (with all its Liquid Glass-y-ness). The display is a 6.8-inch 2868×1320 OLED panel with Honor’s NanoCrystal Shield on top (which is both anti-scratch and anti-reflective), 10,000 nits of peak brightness – somehow –, 1-120Hz adaptive refresh rate support, and a 4,320Hz PWM dimming rate for better eye comfort. There’s an 8,800 mAh battery inside with 100W wired charging and 80W wireless, and the whole phone has IP68, IP69, and IP69K dust/water resistance ratings. 

Honor Magic 9 Pro Max specs

6.8-inch 2868×1320 LTPO OLED display, NanoCrystal glass, 4,320Hz PWM, 10,000 nits peak brightness

Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6

12/256GB, 12/512GB, 16/512GB, 16/1TB

MagicOS 11 based on Android 17

Rear Cameras: 200MP main (f/1.57), 200MP telephoto (f/2.6, 3.5x optical zoom, up to 200x digital zoom), 50MP ultrawide with autofocus

Front Camera: 55MP + 3D depth-sensing camera

8,800 mAh battery, 100W wired charging, 80W wireless charging

IP68/IP69/IP69K

The Magic 9 Pro Max is available today in China, but Honor says global availability is coming soon. Europe, MEA (Middle East & Africa), SEA (Southeast Asia), and “other key international markets” are all confirmed at this point, but there’s no reason to expect this one in the US. 

Honor also launched the Magic 9 in China.

It has a similar design but with a smaller 6.37-inch display, Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5, a very similar camera array, and an 8,000 mAh battery.

title: U.S. government urges Supreme Court to reverse Apple contempt ruling over App Store commission
snippet: Several legal and business groups, in addition to the U.S. government, filed briefs with the Supreme Court this week in the Apple vs. Epic Games lawsuit, urging the justices to reverse at least part of the contempt ruling against Apple. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Several legal and business groups, in addition to the U.S. government, filed briefs with the Supreme Court this week in the Apple vs. Epic Games lawsuit, urging the justices to reverse at least part of the contempt ruling against Apple. Here are the details.

A bit of context

In late June, the U.S. Supreme Court agreed to hear Apple’s argument that a civil contempt ruling against the company should be reversed in its fight against Epic Games.

In essence, when Apple was compelled to allow developers to direct users to external purchasing options, the company did so while imposing a 27% commission on those transactions. When Epic challenged Apple’s implementation, the district court found the company in civil contempt.

Apple has been allowing developers to link to external purchasing options without charging a commission ever since.

Since then, the company has been trying to reverse that ruling, arguing that the actual text of the injunction did not prohibit it from charging a commission, and that lower courts improperly relied on the “spirit of the injunction” to find the company in contempt.

For reference, the original order read:

Apple Inc. and its officers, agents, servants, employees, and any person in active concert or participation with them (“Apple”), are hereby permanently restrained and enjoined from prohibiting developers from (i) including in their apps and their metadata buttons, external links, or other calls to action that direct customers to purchasing mechanisms, in addition to In-App Purchasing and (ii) communicating with customers through points of contact obtained voluntarily from customers through account registration within the app.

Last week, Apple filed its official opening merits brief with the Supreme Court, arguing once again that the contempt ruling should be overturned because the original injunction did not clearly prohibit the company from charging a commission on purchases made outside the App Store.

In its briefing, Apple also argued that allowing the contempt finding to stand would increase the risk of judicial overreach when courts enforce injunctions, leaving companies uncertain about what conduct an order actually prohibits.

U.S. government and other groups weigh in

While Epic Games has until November 13 to file its response, the court this week received a number of amicus briefs (filings from outside interested parties) from the U.S. Department of Justice, through the Solicitor General’s office, along with several legal and business groups weighing in on Apple’s challenge.

In its amicus brief, the Department of Justice argues that “[c]ivil contempt is […] appropriate only if the defendant’s conduct is clearly covered by the injunction’s express terms,” which it says was not the case with Apple’s decision to charge a 27% commission.

It goes on to echo Apple’s argument that civil contempt is improper whenever there is a “fair ground of doubt” as to whether an injunction actually prohibited the conduct at issue, concluding that the Supreme Court “should reverse the contempt finding as to the 27% commission.”

In the same brief, however, the Department of Justice says the lower courts were right to hold Apple in contempt over its “plain button” restriction, arguing that the injunction clearly required Apple to permit both buttons and links, while Apple’s implementation effectively allowed only links.

On the remaining issues, such as restrictions on where external purchase links could appear, the Department of Justice says the Supreme Court should set aside the existing rulings and send them back to the lower courts to be reconsidered under the “fair ground of doubt” standard.

In addition to the Department of Justice, the Supreme Court also received amicus briefs from:

The Chamber of Commerce of the United States

Chamber of Progress

Former Federal Antitrust Enforcers

International Center for Law and Economics (ICLE)

Computer & Communications Industry Association, NetChoice, and Software & Information Industry Association

Washington Legal Foundation (WLF)

In short, they all support the general argument that Apple could not properly be held in civil contempt for conduct that the injunction did not clearly prohibit, and that courts should enforce injunctions based on their actual terms rather than their perceived “spirit.”

The ICLE adds that “choosing a profitable way to comply is still compliance,” while the Former Federal Antitrust Enforcers cited past precedent to argue that having judges determine what commission Apple may charge “is precisely the type of ‘direct price administration’ that ‘antitrust courts normally avoid.’”

Currently, proceedings are underway in the district court to determine how much, if any, commission Apple may charge on linked-out purchases, while the Supreme Court reviews the contempt ruling itself.

title: iPhone Duo video shows left-handed use for new model
snippet: iPhone Duo is less than a month away, but many prospective buyers are still wondering how well the device will work in left-handed use. Here’s a video that shows a left-handed example. more…
fullText:
iPhone Duo is less than a month away, but many prospective buyers are still wondering how well the device will work in left-handed use. Here’s a video that shows a left-handed example.

Here’s how iPhone Duo works in left-handed use

If you’re left-handed, the iPhone Duo may be exciting but also spark some questions. That’s because the new foldable is clearly designed for right-handed use primarily.

When using the outer display, iPhone Duo’s left side is one straight flat edge because it’s where the hinge is. But the right side has curved corners, inviting you to open it like a book.

The dock is also located on the right side of the display, and Apple hasn’t said if an accessibility setting will let you move it to the left.

So how will left-handed users fare with the iPhone Duo? 

Since everyone’s hand size is different, testing the device in an Apple Store will be the only way to know for sure. But I recently came across a video of iPhone Duo being used left-handed, and it’s the first time I’ve seen someone try it.

Here’s the video from Tom Hitchins (@bytereview) on Instagram:

Hitchins looks a little uncomfortable with the device, but as he explains in the comments, that’s because he’s actually right-handed. Thus, his left-handed test was for others’ sake.

	

The video says “works well enough” as Hitchins is able to reach from the left side all the way to the dock on the right. But you’ll want to test yourself to be sure.

I’m right-handed, but use my iPhone in my left hand so that my dominant hand is kept free. I suspect there are plenty of other right-handed users who do the same. So I’m a little unsure about the adjustment to using iPhone Duo in my right hand, but will report back once I’m able to test it.

title: Apple Wallet in iOS 27 adds feature that’s been on my wishlist for years
snippet: iOS 27 adds a variety of new features and changes for Apple Wallet, including one that’s been on my wishlist for years: the ability to import physical passes. more…
fullText:
iOS 27 adds a variety of new features and changes for Apple Wallet, including one that’s been on my wishlist for years: the ability to import physical passes.

iOS 27 lets you import physical passes, membership cards, event tickets into Apple Wallet

Apple Wallet offers a host of features to help you replace your physical wallet and keys.

It holds credit cards, driver’s licenses, transit cards, boarding passes, event tickets, car keys, home keys, hotel keys, and more.

And with iOS 27, the Wallet app takes another big step toward being the only wallet you need.

That’s because you can now import physical passes, tickets, membership cards, and the like into Apple Wallet.

Here’s how it works, per Apple:

iPhone and Apple Watch users will be able to create and store passes in Apple Wallet from physical cards, like loyalty or membership cards, eliminating the need to fumble through pockets and bags. With Siri mode in the Camera app, users simply point their iPhone at any physical card with a barcode or even screenshot a digital one, and they’ll be prompted to save it to Apple Wallet. Users can also create and add a pass directly from Apple Wallet. Once added, passes are ready to present as a barcode or QR code right from their iPhone or Apple Watch.

Digital passes are a lot more common today than when Apple Wallet first launched. But they aren’t available for everything.

I definitely still encounter businesses and events that utilize physical passes exclusively. And when I do, it adds a little anxiety to my life because I then need to remember to bring those passes with me at the right time.

But with iOS 27, everything can start going in the Wallet app, which is always with me. By putting everything in Wallet, the mental burden of remembering to bring something extra is suddenly gone.

title: Qualcomm announces the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6
snippet: Qualcomm today announced the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 to power the next generation of Android smartphones. more…
fullText:
Qualcomm today announced the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6 and Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6 to power the next generation of Android smartphones.

The big change this year is how there are a pair of chips. Qualcomm considers both to be “flagship” offerings that give “OEMs greater choice.” The Elite Gen 6 is seen as the follow-up to last year’s Elite Gen 5, while the Elite Extreme Gen 6 comes in a level higher.

Both are built on a 2nm process with an Oryon CPU that has two 5GHz Prime Cores and six 4GHz Performance cores. The 8 Elite Gen 6 offers 10% improved CPU performance and a 37% gain in power efficiency compared to the Gen 5. 

On the 8 Elite Extreme, CPU performance improves by 13% compared to last generation. A global VVC (H.266) codec on the Extreme allows for more power-efficient video. 

	

A “rearchitected” Adreno GPU offers 35% improved GPU performance and 40% power efficiency improvement over the Gen 5.

On the Extreme, there are AI-dedicated Adreno matrix cores that allow for more advanced models to run. GPU performance improves 44% compared to last year. There’s also 18 MB of High Performance Memory that compared to last generation offers a 12% power improvement. For gaming, Adreno Neural Fusion uses the new GPU matrix cores for AI super-resolution and frame generation, which makes possible up to 40% power savings in supported games.

The Hexagon NPU features a new Element Accelerator for transformer workloads to benefit LLMs. There’s 14% improved NPU performance and 20% improved AI performance-per-watt with the 12 scalar + 8 vector + 1 tensor + 1 element configuration.

On the 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6, a 50% larger shared memory allows for 30B+ parameters Mixture of Experts (MoE) models. The aim is to reduce trips to external memory, with 35% improved NPU performance and 33% improved AI  performance-per-watt. 

The Spectra ISP features what Qualcomm calls Intelligent Pixel Control to understand scenes on a per-pixel level. On the Extreme, you have support for 8K60 video and 4K240 ultra HD slow-motion capture. 

Both chips are paired with the Qualcomm X105 5G modem that is “newly architected” for greater downlink (10% increase) and uplink speeds. Specifically, six antennas can capture multiple data streams at once. This supports 3GPP Release 19 5G Advanced.

Motorola today announced the Signature 27 with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Extreme Gen 6. More on that here.

Note: Qualcomm paid for travel and accommodations for this launch event, but had no input on editorial content.

title: Google Messages finally rolls out new long-press menu with precise copying
snippet: After testing got underway in January, Google Messages is finally widely rolling out a new long-press menu in conversations. more…
fullText:
After testing got underway in January, Google Messages is finally widely rolling out a new long-press menu in conversations.

This new design replaces the top toolbar that housed various actions. Google only surfaced three actions with everything else in an overflow menu.

	

Upon long-pressing on a chat message or image, Google will show a floating menu with Remix (photos), Reply, Forward, Copy (text), Star, Delete, Select more, Info, and Save (photos).

Each action is accompanied by an icon at the front for quick scanning, while Copy lets you highlight a specific part of the message by pressing down and dragging the bubble. Previously, you could only copy the entire message.

	

If you’ve selected the newest message in a thread, Google will somewhat center it with a bouncy animation and haptic feedback. Messages prominently blurs the background layer when this menu is active. The row of emoji and “Create” Photomoji shortcuts is unchanged.

As of today, we’re seeing the new Google Messages long-press menu widely rolled out with stable version 20260910_03_RC02. There is a server-side component, so be sure to Force stop from the App info menu if it’s not yet live.

title: Motorola’s wide Galaxy Z Fold 8 competitor might be very tiny and called ‘Razr Flex’
snippet: According to a new leak, Motorola’s upcoming entry in the wide, book-style foldable space may be called “Razr Flex” and pack some very familiar specs. more…
fullText:
According to a new leak, Motorola’s upcoming entry in the wide, book-style foldable space may be called “Razr Flex” and pack some very familiar specs.

Specs for Motorola’s wide foldable were shared by Android Headlines alongside a possible name for the device – “Razr Flex.” That’s apparently the name being used internally around the device, so it’s unclear if that would be used as a consumer-facing name. The codename is “Parker,” the report claims.

Much more interesting are the details around the side of this foldable, which shares the same general form factor as Samsung’s smash hit Galaxy Z Fold 8, just in a much smaller footprint. Apparently, the outer display is just 4.97-inches in size – the Galaxy Z Fold 8 is 5.5-inches – while the inner display is less than 7-inches across. Very tiny by modern phone standards, even in this new form factor.

The leaked specs include:

	

4.97-inch outer display (1736×1140)

6.92-inch inner display (2364×1728)

110x149x5.8mm unfolded | 110x76x12.6mm folded

215g

Snapdragon 8 Gen 5

12GB RAM

256GB of storage

5,000 mAh battery with Qi2 (magnets unclear)

IP48/49

50MP main/50MP ultrawide rear cameras, 32MP selfie cameras

PANTONE Coriander, PANTONE Dark Botanical Garden

It’s important to stress just how much smaller this is compared to other wide foldables. iPhone Duo is thicker and heavier than Samsung’s phone, but has roughly the same screen sizes. The closest comparison is the Xiaomi 18 Fold, which has a 5.38-inch outer display, but even that still has a 7.58-inch inner panel. 

The specs are otherwise pretty familiar to the full-size Razr Fold that launched earlier this year.

Concept renders were also shared, but they’re explicitly not based on, well, anything except sketches and Motorola’s general design language – take them not just with a grain of salt, but maybe a whole container.

The “Razr Flex” is said to be launching this year with a “mid-December” debut mentioned.

There’s also Pixel Watch sleep sync that pauses music, disables touch controls, and silences notifications on the Pixel Buds. title: Samsung open-ear Galaxy Buds On images show what they look like when worn
snippet: Once rumored to go by a different name, Samsung’s Galaxy Buds On open-ear designs have appeared with a little more detail in new images, suggesting these earbuds might become official sooner rather than later. more…
fullText:
Once rumored to go by a different name, Samsung’s Galaxy Buds On open-ear designs have appeared with a little more detail in new images, suggesting these earbuds might become official sooner rather than later.

The Galaxy Buds On have been leaked several times over the last couple of months, though rumors suggested the earbuds would go by “Galaxy Buds Able” instead of the “Galaxy Buds On” name. That information was gleaned from Samsung’s Wearable app in early July, though the first of the two names seems to be an internal moniker.

New images of the Galaxy Buds On have surfaced (via Android Headlines). Previously, we’ve seen detailed renders and icon images, but nothing that looks like it could be official from Samsung. The new photos look a little cleaner, and one looks likely to be from the marketing team.

The Galaxy Buds On images also show what they look like when worn properly – that is, clipped around the ears rather than resting in them. It’s also a different style from the open-ear design worn over the ear. They look uncomfortable, but the design is already plentiful in certain regions, suggesting it’s a popular form factor.

	

It’s hard to pick up any details from the earbud images or to determine which port is the driver and which is the microphone for ambient noise detection. Even if that were determined properly, there’s no telling how they’ll sound prior to release.

The Galaxy Buds On were reported to have a few interesting features when previous images were leaked, such as an “Auto Volume” setting and head-nod and shake gesture control. Samsung Galaxy users will also have voice memos automatically transcribed to text.

Other devices like the Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra have been circulating alongside the Galaxy Buds On, suggesting Samsung is gearing up for another launch soon. When that is, there’s no telling right now.

title: Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra leak shows another side, confirming minimal changes
snippet: The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra showed up in a leak in August, but a new one has surfaced as the October launch date gets closer. The most recent images further confirm little about the design will change. more…
fullText:
The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra showed up in a leak in August, but a new one has surfaced as the October launch date gets closer. The most recent images further confirm little about the design will change.

The last leak image we saw of the Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra confirmed the new tablet will carry on Samsung’s recent camera notch design change. It takes on a teardrop shape, minimizing its scree footprint. That, along with the S Pen changed with the release of the Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra.

In comparing leaks with new ones courtesy of Evan Blass on Twitter/X, it still seems like nothing on the outside is being altered. The new leak provides side and rear views – something the previous leak left out. But it only further confirms the Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra will carry on the Galaxy Tab S11 Ultra’s build design.

That even goes for the S Pen charging location, which docks to the top right, when the Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra is in its landscape orientation.

	

That carry over from last year isn’t a bad thing, and tablets have sort of stagnated for some time. That’s part of the reason foldables have become so popular in recent years.

But Samsung has stuck to this design philosophy for some time. It might be nice to see some change that improves on bezels, or battery life. Of course, this leak only shows off what’s on the outside.

The Galaxy Tab S12 Ultra is expected to launch on October 7.

title: iOS 27 gives Apple Mail my most wished for feature upgrade
snippet: Apple’s Mail app in iOS 27 includes the feature upgrade that’s been at the top of my wishlist for years: search that “just works.” more…
fullText:
Apple’s Mail app in iOS 27 includes the feature upgrade that’s been at the top of my wishlist for years: search that “just works.”

iOS 27 overhauls search in Apple Mail to make it more relevant and accurate

Apple’s Mail app has long been plagued by lackluster search. 

I suspect that statement won’t be controversial at all among years-long users of the app. In fact, some might say “lackluster” is too kind a word to use.

But Apple says iOS 27 finally brings the Apple Mail search upgrade the app deserves.

From Apple’s website detailing iOS 27’s new features:

More relevant search in Mail. A new ranking system brings the most relevant results to the top to help you find what you need right away — even if it’s buried deep in your inbox.

Here’s how this new ranking system in Mail will benefit users.

When you first open search in iOS 27’s Mail app, there’s a banner at the top that highlights “Expanded Search Results.” It explains: “Mail can look for more results based on what you mean, not just the words you type.”

Essentially, Apple is bringing search into the 21st century. Or you could say, it’s making search work the way it always should have.

I’ve used iOS 27 in beta for several months, and in my experience it’s definitely an upgrade over the old system. There hasn’t been a single time that I’ve tried searching for something and couldn’t find it. But understandably, your mileage may vary.

The improved search relies on proper indexing, so if your iPhone is still performing indexing (check the Settings app to see if it’s “Optimizing Search & Siri”), you may need to wait a bit before search works as well as it should.

What’s your take on Apple Mail’s search capabilities today? Have you tried the iOS 27 version yet? Let us know in the comments.

title: iOS 27 Lets You Do Check Splitting and Custom Cards in Apple Wallet
snippet: New features include creating a Wallet card from a physical business card or scanning a receipt to split the bill.
fullText:
If you frequently get stuck footing the whole bill when you dine out with friends, you might have a new tool that can help: Apple Wallet in iOS 27 can split the bill from a camera image of a receipt.

The feature uses Apple Intelligence to make items on the receipt selectable so you can quickly determine what’s yours (and not yours) and what’s owed. It’s one of several new Wallet features that Apple previewed at its annual software event, WWDC, back in June, that are now rolling out. Those new features include being able to create custom Wallet items from scanned physical cards or from scratch, and view recurring payments if you have an Apple Card.

For iOS 27, Apple also announced new features for developers geared to Apple Wallet, including the ability to make posters for multiticket events and adding order tracking for retail apps using Apple Intelligence.

			

More from CNET

How to use the new check-splitting feature

New iOS 27 Wallet features include the ability to scan a receipt and then split the bill with others.

Apple/Screenshot by CNET

Before you can take advantage of some of these new Wallet features, you’ll need to make sure your device is using iOS 27.

Receipt splitting in Wallet starts with using the new Siri mode in the Camera app. If you’re pointing your lens at a receipt, a prompt for Split Bill With Apple Cash will come up. You can go through your contacts to search for people you want to split the check with, but they’ll need to be able to pay with Apple Cash. 

Apple Wallet will show a list of the items ordered, and you can select from that list, then choose how you want the bill split and how much to tip. Apple Wallet can’t force your friends to pay; it’s not a collection agency.

How to use the new custom Wallet items feature

To add a Wallet item from a business card, or just create a digital Wallet card without one, tap the plus icon at the top to add something new.

You’ll have the option to scan a debit, credit, transit or other type of ID card, or you can choose Create a Pass to work off a business card.

Apple Wallet now allows you to create digital passes from physical cards in iOS 27.

Apple/Screenshot by CNET

CNET Senior Writer and iOS features expert Zachary McAuliffe said this feature has already worked well for him. 

“I digitized my gym membership card, and it’s worked great,” McAuliffe said. “I was worried the scanner wouldn’t pick up my iPhone’s screen, but the scanner seemingly picks up my screen better than my old card. I also appreciate how this saves me space on my already crowded keyring.”

Editing the details of a custom Wallet card allows you to either import the contents of a scanned card and edit them, or just enter your own details. Apple Wallet offers a few different templates for custom Wallet items, and you can adjust the color or background. Item details can be edited later if the information changes or you make a mistake. Newer Apple Watch models should be able to pin these custom digital passes using the Smart Stack feature.

To view recurring payments on your Apple Card, just tap on the Card in Wallet and use the three dots on the top right to select it from the menu.

More iOS 27 Wallet features are likely to roll out as Apple continues releasing updates to its new operating system.

He lives in the Texas Hill Country.

In recent years, Macs had been getting more and more affordable. Cheaper starting points, more memory and storage per dollar, and the introduction of MacBook Neo. For the first time, Apple had started to become one of the best values on the market.

Unfortunately, Apple just drastically increased its prices because of the ongoing memory shortage. Macs aren’t as appealing as they were a few months ago, that said, there’s still some decent deals out there – and if you’re in need of a new computer, I’d still say todays Macs are a good value against the rest of the computing market.

MacBook Air

Up until the launch of MacBook Neo, the MacBook Air represented the entry point to Apple’s laptop lineup. Despite MacBook Neo making its value proposition slightly questionable, I’d still say MacBook Air is a great laptop if you want a better experience without needing anything premium.

MagSafe, a P3 color display, Center Stage on the webcam, and more battery life are just a few of the highlights with MacBook Air. It also comes with a 15-inch size variant, unlike MacBook Neo which only offers 13-inch.

title: Apple Watch Series 12 one week later: There’s so much more than meets the eye
snippet: When Apple unveiled the Apple Watch Series 12, two features stood out: the new Siri Recap feature, as well as the much improved heart rate monitor. While those two features were part of the reason I was compelled to buy the new Apple Watch, I’ve found myself delighted by much more than just those two things. more…
fullText:
When Apple unveiled the Apple Watch Series 12, two features stood out: the new Siri Recap feature, as well as the much improved heart rate monitor. While those two features were part of the reason I was compelled to buy the new Apple Watch, I’ve found myself delighted by much more than just those two things.

Battery and charging

While Apple’s website doesn’t quote any additional battery life for Apple Watch Series 12 compared to Series 11, the battery certainly feels like it lasts longer. As I’ve written in the past, I was someone who used the WHOOP prior to the Apple Watch Series 12, and even though I kept my Apple Watch, I never used it for sleep tracking.

After the keynote, I decided to give Apple Watch sleep tracking a shot. That said, on my Series 11, juggling sleep tracking and charging was a bit of a pain. After using the watch throughout the day, I’d have to charge it a little bit before going to sleep, then when I wake up, I’d have to charge it again.

On Series 12, that isn’t the case. It has enough battery to last through a day and overnight, and now I just charge it when I wake up. Apple Watch Series 12 also charges significantly faster, which makes that part less of a pain. 15 minutes of charging gets you up to 12 hours of use, per Apple.

I imagine the new S11 chip, derived from the A20 Pro’s 2nm design, is a large part of the reason why battery life feels so much longer. Regardless of the why, it feels amazing to not have charging anxiety around sleep tracking on the Apple Watch Series 12. Another big upside to the S11 chip? Apple Watch Series 12 feels so much faster, especially with Siri.

Software exclusives

On Series 12, Apple finally includes a proper step counter as a complication, which I like checking on in my smart stack. Could this come to older Apple Watches? Probably. It’s not like Apple didn’t count steps before. Apple Watch Series 12 certainly counts them more accurately, but given the fact that the data is there, I think Apple should just add the complication. Either way, it’s nice to have on Series 12.

Another neat new feature is the entire Readiness app, which gives you an idea of how okay you’re doing today based on last night’s sleep, your previous day’s activity, and your vitals. This is similar to a recovery score on WHOOP, and I was certainly happy to see Apple add this to the Apple Watch? It’s a bit of a bummer it’s exclusive to the Series 12, but I could understand why Apple isn’t willing to calculate it with less accurate data.

Wrap up

All in all, the Apple Watch Series 12 is a rather nice upgrade. It’s a total S year, but if you care about your Apple Watch actually doing more rather than just looking different, I’d say this might be one of the most substantial year over year upgrades since Apple Watch Series 4.

The bezels certainly got a slight bit thicker compared to Series 10 and 11. As someone who uses a watch face with a black background, I can’t say I’ve noticed this much – though I hope Apple improves on this in the next iteration.

One last thing of note: Apple Watch Series 12 offers Ceramic Shield 2 on the aluminum models, making it hold up to scratches much better than older Apple Watch models. I haven’t owned mine long enough to truly test this, though so far my Apple Watch still looks perfect.

title: This Comically Dark PSA Pushes Back Against Big Tech Enshittification
snippet: Cory Doctorow and the Norwegian Consumer Council are behind a hilarious and insightful ad campaign about how everything’s getting worse.
fullText:
Imagine, if you will, a pale figure of Death, dressed in a black robe holding a scythe, alongside a handsome, lumberjack-looking Nordic fella who goes by the name Enshittificator. As partners in crime, they conspire to make your life suck, all because they have the power to make digital products and services worse. 

If that piques your interest — and maybe sounds too much like real life — a new “anti-enshittification” ad campaign is worth a few minutes of your time.

The term “enshittification” was popularized in 2022 by author and activist Cory Doctorow, and its massive cultural surge earned it a place in Merriam-Webster’s slang hub last year. Enshittification is a deliberate process, designed by companies to maximize profit. 

			

More from CNET

It starts with luring you to a product or service, then making it so good that you become completely dependent on it. The next step is to pull the rug out from under you by hiding basic features behind a paywall, reducing overall quality and squeezing you for every last dime while providing as little value as possible. 

The Death and Enshittificator video above, released on YouTube in mid-September, is the second of a series from the Norwegian Consumer Council, an independent, government-funded nonprofit that advocates for consumer rights. The main character, the Enshittificator, is a bearded Nordic man who says in the first video, released in February, that his “job is to make things shitty.” 

The initial video concludes with Mr. Enshittificator getting into a car accident because he didn’t pay a subscription for his braking system, a scenario he appeared to find amusing. In the second video, he meets Death in the hospital, and the two enter into a business relationship. (He now dons a yellow hazmat suit to stay alive.) 

The duo spends time making every conceivable product worse, from TVs and toothbrushes to smartphone storage. They point out that products with long lifespans, like the famously indestructible Nokia 3310 — which makes a cameo appearance — only generate revenue once. If companies want a profitable business model, however, they have to use low-quality materials, ensure products can’t be fixed and stop issuing updates. 

“Look at all the companies that used to make solid products,” the Enshittificator said. “Where are they now?”

“Dead,” Death said, and they share a knowing smile. 

The Norwegian Consumer Council’s ads are part of its Breaking Free initiative, a multipronged policy approach to make technology work in favor of consumers, rather than against them. The campaign craftily relies on dark humor to detail how enshittification affects everyday life, from paid subscription models to planned obsolescence, which forces you to buy newer devices. 

The videos are also a strikingly accurate commentary on the dismal state of products and gadgets in the digital age. Prices go up while reliability plummets. Companies rely on shady advertising tactics and dodge consumer protection rights. 

Doctorow himself collaborated with the nonprofit to help launch the series, which he’s immensely pleased with. In an email to CNET, he said, “The idea that firms’ market power means that they can worsen their offerings with impunity, combined with the minor license to vulgarity of my dirty little word, have proven a winning combination for helping people direct their anger in the right direction.”

Real life (and death)

It would not be shocking if there were actual board rooms that looked like this.Norwegian Consumer Council

The enshittification process is relatable and real. In 2020, Apple agreed to pay up to $500 million to settle the landmark “batterygate” class action lawsuit over allegations that it secretly slowed down older iPhone models through software updates. Powerful tech companies have poured massive amounts of money into lobbying against right-to-repair laws, preventing customers from fixing their own devices when they break.  

“It’s really important that the products can’t be fixed,” said the Enshittificator. “It breaks, then it dies, so you have to buy a new one. And another one. And another one. And another one. And another one.”

“This way, we’re actually slowly killing the planet as well,” a smiling Death said, helpfully chiming in. 

The videos also satirize how digital services slowly degrade over time. In one scene, the Enshittificator tells an employee, “The 1,000 pictures of your deceased mother are mine, and you’re going to pay for them.” It’s a direct nod to Google Photos’ 2021 policy shift, which ended free unlimited storage and capped free accounts at 15GB, requiring users to get a subscription to keep already uploaded photos on the platform. 

Another scene takes a jab at automakers who sell you basic functionality as an add-on subscription service. 

“I don’t have any more money. You have me in the palm of your hand,” said the Enshittificator in a fake presentation about selling cars. “You can crush me. So what do you do? Updates. Radio? Premium feature. Heating? Premium feature. Now I have a shitty car, and I can’t afford a new one, but what I can afford is a small monthly payment!”

This is a reference to BMW’s controversial microtransaction model, where it tried to make heated seats and other in-car features part of a subscription plan. While intense consumer backlash forced the German automaker to walk back some of the “add-ons,” several features remain behind a paywall. Other brands have followed suit — Hyundai’s BlueLink and Kia Connect require paid plans to use remote start. For a period, both manufacturers even omitted the remote-start button from the physical key fob, completely blocking owners from using the feature for free.

Can it be fixed?

It’s important, though a little depressing, to imagine how much better life would be if companies actually invested money into making their products better, safer and longer-lasting — and not just more profitable for them. 

In its Breaking Free: Pathways to a Fair Technological Future report, the Norwegian Consumer Council argues that major tech business models “are often fundamentally incompatible with consumer and human rights.” To dismantle the “walled gardens run by Big Tech feudalists” and end dependence on Big Tech, the nonprofit is pushing for policy reforms built around a three-pronged strategy based on democratic values and principles of openness. 

The first is interoperability, which would force platforms to interface with one another. This is already taking shape under the EU’s Digital Markets Act, which required Apple to allow third-party app stores and mandated Meta to support external chats in WhatsApp, 

Next comes portability, which would allow users to move their contacts, content, photos and anything else to rival services. A subscriber fed up with Spotify adding AI features, for instance, would be able to switch to YouTube Music or Apple Music without losing their saved playlists, thereby eliminating platform lock-in. 

Finally, and arguably the most difficult to implement, is decentralization of social media, which could shift social media away from single-entity corporate control toward open networks like the Fediverse (which powers platforms such as Mastodon). Though still evolving as protocols develop, decentralization enhances interoperability, making cross-network movement frictionless.

Reining in Big Tech remains an uphill battle, but in the meantime, the campaign offers a hilarious — and painfully accurate — look at the modern digital hellscape.

“The true mark of success for a project like this is when other people pick it up and run with it,” Doctorow said.

title: Watch UEFA Nations League Soccer: Livestream Turkey vs. France From Anywhere
snippet: Zinedine Zidane takes charge of Les Bleus for the first time in İzmit.
fullText:
French soccer legend Zinedine Zidane begins his tenure as Les Bleus’ head coach on Friday with a tricky first test in the UEFA Nations League away to Turkey.

Zidane has big boots to fill, succeeding his former teammate Didier Deschamps, who consistently led the French to the latter stages of major tournaments throughout his 14 years in charge, notably winning the World Cup in 2018.

Zidane’s first job will be to lift his players after the disappointment of losing in the semifinal to Spain in this summer’s World Cup — a tournament they had looked well placed to win after making a superb start to the competition. fullText:

title: Apple TV has too many good shows on now and I can’t keep up
snippet: Apple TV has been called “the new HBO” for its focus on quality over quantity. But recently, the streamer has starting ramping its lineup of shows I want to watch, and I can’t keep up. more…
fullText:
Apple TV has been called “the new HBO” for its focus on quality over quantity. But recently, the streamer has starting ramping its lineup of shows I want to watch, and I can’t keep up.

Apple TV’s quality and quantity have ramped up as streamer hits new stride

I’ve subscribed to Apple TV since it first debuted in 2019, and the streamer has typically had 1-2 shows on at a time that I’ve wanted to watch.

This kind of output resembles HBO, which has built its brand creating fewer, but generally higher-quality shows than most competitors.

In the last couple years though, Apple’s output has been slowly growing, and at the same time its batting average has arguably improved too.

The result? Apple has too many good shows on right now, and I can’t keep up.

Currently airing every week on Apple TV are new episodes of:

Ted Lasso, one of my favorite shows

Slow Horses, another all-time best Apple series

Dark Matter, a sci-fi series I loved the first season of, yet haven’t started the second

Brothers, a new half-hour comedy with Matthew McConaughey and Woody Harrelson that looks fun

Last Seen, a new thriller I’ve heard great things about but haven’t watched

plus Women in Blue and Knife Edge, both of which I might watch in a slower season but right now they’re low priorities

I’m excited to dive into Dark Matter, as season 1 made it one of my favorite sci-fi shows just behind Severance and Pluribus. But it’s been hard to find time to start season 2. And I’m always up for a comfort watch half-hour comedy, so Brothers is in the queue.

I love crime thrillers and dramas involving family, so Last Seen looks very much like my kind of show. But I haven’t started it yet, despite Stephen King’s endorsement.

Two observations about LAST SEEN, 4 episodes in (Apple+): 1–It's a fantastic show, and 2–I see no good resolution for the families involved. Or for Sarah, who is played beautifully by Chloe Jean Lourdes.

— Stephen King (@StephenKing) September 24, 2026

And these are only the shows currently airing. 

I’m still not caught up on Silo season 3, and haven’t even started Sugar season 2 despite great reviews and being a fan of the show. I could watch more on Apple if I ignored other streamers, but other shows elsewhere are keeping me busy too.

	

October is right around the corner too, and Apple has a whopping seven new TV shows and movies premiering—the most I can remember in a single month.

All this to say, I’m really pleased that Apple TV is doing so well. It won more Emmys than HBO this year for a reason.

What’s your view on Apple TV’s current and recent shows? Let us know in the comments.

fullText:
Apple today updated its official list of digital camera RAW formats supported across its platforms, adding support for 11 models from several manufacturers. Here are the details.

Apple now supports RAW files from 562 cameras

Apple’s operating systems offer system-level support for RAW images captured by many third-party cameras.

In a nutshell, this lets compatible apps work directly with those cameras’ RAW files, allowing them to better adjust elements such as exposure, color, and so on.

That is in contrast with formats such as JPEG, which don’t allow for the same post-processing editing flexibility, since much of that image processing is basically baked into the final image.

Apple maintains support articles listing digital cameras with RAW formats supported by its current (and past) operating systems. The list was updated today, adding 11 digital cameras, bringing the total to 562 models.

title: Here’s what I’d like to see Apple do right in a screenless fitness tracker
snippet: Last week, Bloomberg reported that Apple is working on a screenless fitness tracker, akin to a WHOOP or Fitbit Air. As someone who’s used the WHOOP for the past 6 months, I do think its a great concept, though there are a few things I’d like to see Apple do better. more…
fullText:
Last week, Bloomberg reported that Apple is working on a screenless fitness tracker, akin to a WHOOP or Fitbit Air. As someone who’s used the WHOOP for the past 6 months, I do think its a great concept, though there are a few things I’d like to see Apple do better.

We don’t have many details on what Apple’s screenless fitness tracker will look like, as the product is relatively early in development. At the earliest, it would debut in 2028. Bloomberg describes it as a “thin fabric band with a sensor-equipped computing module.”

Earlier this year, WHOOP and Chase had a promo where you could get a discounted or free WHOOP if you had a Sapphire card, and I took advantage of that. Since then, I’ve been a WHOOP user – though I never went all in on it.

The reasoning for that was simple: automatic workout detection will never be perfect, and I found it annoying to have to pull out my phone to log a workout, whether that be beforehand or retroactively. With the Apple Watch, you can just start the workout on the screen, and the WHOOP will sync the times from Apple Health. This was the main reason I kept wearing my Apple Watch. 

For gym workouts, pulling out your phone might be fine, but for casual biking for long walks I’d rather not have to fiddle with my phone.

So, for Apple’s screenless fitness tracker, I’d love to see some sort of button and indicator LED that you can use for starting and stopping a workout. You’d still need to go on your phone later to categorize the workout, but I’d much rather do that than have to deal with it in the moment. Apple could also develop a classification model based on certain factors.

Wrap up

If Apple managed to develop a screenless fitness tracker that didn’t feel like a pain to use without a phone, I think it’d be quite compelling. The form factor has many advantages, including comfort, battery life, and the ability to wear it alongside a traditional watch.

	

Personally, after evaluating the WHOOP, I do think I prefer just having a smartwatch, even with the battery life disadvantages. I do understand wanting something screenless so its distraction-free, but personally I just enable Do Not Disturb on my watch.
